raw_case_text:
We are reporting a 32-year-old woman known to have diabetes mellitus who presented to the emergency department initially with a 2-week history of abdominal distention and increased abdominal girth associated with shortness of breath. She denied any nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, early satiety or unintentional weight loss, hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia. The patient denied any past surgical history. She was born and raised in the USA and never traveled outside the USA. Her social history was significant for active tobacco and marijuana smoking. She had no known allergies. Her initial vitals were blood pressure of 131/79 mm Hg, a pulse of 83 bpm, respiratory rate of 18, and temperature of 98.6 F. On examination, the abdomen was soft and distended with positive shifting dullness. Bowel sounds were normal.
Computed tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast showed a large amount of ascites with normal hepatic architecture. Ultrasound of the pelvis showed large-volume ascites and normal appearing ovaries and uterus. The patient underwent paracentesis showing a low SAAG value (of 1 and repeat 0.6) with high protein (6.4 and repeat 7), neutrophilic predominance initially (total WBCs 6,760 with 95% neutrophils), then lymphocytic predominance (total WBCs 3,840 with 64% lymphocytes); cytology of ascitic fluid was negative for any malignant cells. Of note, she was found to have an adenosine deaminase (ADA) level of 113 in ascitic fluid; upon repeat testing, the level was 100.6. Acid-fast staining, MTB PCR, and mycobacterium cultures were negative in ascitic fluid. Ascitic fluid amylase level was 46 U/L, TAG level was 22 mg/dL, and LDH level was 554 U/L. HIV testing, HCV testing, HAV IgM, and auto-immune workup, including ANA, ANCA vasculitis antibodies, anti-smooth muscle antibodies, and liver kidney microsomal antibodies, were also negative. Serum pro-BNP was 40 pg/mL, lipase 37 U/L, ceruloplasmin level 38 mg/dL, alpha-1-antitrypsin level 144 mg/dL, ESR 100 mm/h, and CRP was 85 mg/L. Her serum immunofixation showed a dense polyclonal pattern suggestive of chronic inflammation. Urine testing for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae was negative. CT of the chest and CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast material were negative for any malignant focus. She underwent exploratory abdominal laparoscopy, which revealed fibrinous exudate on the peritoneal surface, and had a biopsy of the peritoneum. The pathology report from the peritoneal biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with no malignancy (Fig. 1). PAP smear showed atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance. Endometrial biopsy was also negative for any malignancy. Transvaginal ultrasound showed normal ovaries. She also had EGD and colonoscopy to rule out gastrointestinal malignancy and in view of the unknown origin of ascites. EGD and colonoscopy both were unremarkable, and biopsy reports were negative for any malignancy. The patient was lost to follow-up, and treatment was not initiated.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old female with diabetes mellitus presented with a 2-week history of progressive abdominal distention, increased abdominal girth, and shortness of breath.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 2-week history of rapidly increasing abdominal distention and dyspnea. She denied fever, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, early satiety, unintentional weight loss, or gastrointestinal bleeding.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Active cigarette and marijuana smoking. Born and raised in the United States without foreign travel history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reported abdominal distention and dyspnea. Denied fevers, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits. Home medications: unmentioned. Allergies: no known drug allergies.

objective.physical_examination: Blood pressure 131/79 mmHg, pulse 83 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, body temperature 98.6 °F (37.0 °C). Abdominal examination revealed significant abdominal distention with positive shifting dullness; abdomen was soft and nontender with normal bowel sounds.
objective.routine_investigations: Inflammatory markers: ESR 100 mm/h, CRP 85 mg/L. Serum immunofixation: dense polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia. Serum chemistry & biomarkers: pro-BNP 40 pg/mL, lipase 37 U/L, ceruloplasmin 38 mg/dL, alpha-1-antitrypsin 144 mg/dL. Serologies: HIV, hepatitis C, and hepatitis A IgM were negative; autoimmune panel (ANA, ANCA, anti-smooth muscle, and liver-kidney microsomal antibodies) was negative. Urine PCR for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae was negative. Chest CT scan: normal without pulmonary lesions.
objective.advanced_workup: CT scan of abdomen and pelvis with contrast: large-volume ascites with normal liver parenchymal architecture and no mass lesions. Pelvic and transvaginal ultrasound: large ascites with normal uterus and bilateral ovaries. Diagnostic paracentesis: revealed exudative ascites with low SAAG (1.0 and repeat 0.6) and high total protein (6.4 g/dL and repeat 7.0 g/dL); cell count demonstrated initial neutrophilia (total WBC 6,760/uL with 95% neutrophils) transitioning to lymphocytic predominance (total WBC 3,840/uL with 64% lymphocytes); ascitic amylase 46 U/L, triglycerides 22 mg/dL, LDH 554 U/L, and adenosine deaminase (ADA) markedly elevated at 113 U/L (repeat 100.6 U/L); ascitic cytology was negative for malignant cells; ascitic fluid AFB smear, MTB PCR, and mycobacterial cultures were negative. Upper endoscopy (EGD) and colonoscopy: unremarkable mucosal appearance with non-malignant mucosal biopsies. Endometrial biopsy: negative for malignancy. Exploratory abdominal laparoscopy: revealed dense fibrinous exudates across peritoneal surfaces; peritoneal biopsy demonstrated granulomatous inflammation without malignant cells.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Peritoneal tuberculosis presenting with marked exudative ascites. Supported by markedly elevated ascitic adenosine deaminase (ADA 113 U/L and 100.6 U/L), high-protein low-SAAG exudative fluid with lymphocytic predominance, and laparoscopic peritoneal biopsy demonstrating granulomatous inflammation; ascitic fluid AFB stain, MTB PCR, and mycobacterial cultures were negative. Peritoneal carcinomatosis, ovarian cancer, cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and autoimmune peritonitis were thoroughly ruled out.
Treatment & Outcome: Antitubercular therapy was indicated based on histological and biochemical confirmation; however, the patient was lost to follow-up prior to therapy initiation.
